pull.title: fix(config-dir): only mcc-migrate ever moves ~/.fcc, and repair what 6.40.0 left behind
pull.body:
6.40.0 renamed the config directory to `~/.mcc` and shipped the migration around it half-finished: the Get Started button could never render, `--force` was dead code, one transient `sqlite3` error could silently start an existing user on an empty `~/.mcc`, a test ran `mcc-migrate` against the developer's real home, and 19 code spans in README/USAGE were corrupted by the mechanical rename while the three new names it introduced were documented nowhere.

This is the follow-up. The organising rule is the one the user set:

> **The only way `~/.fcc` becomes `~/.mcc` is running `mcc-migrate`.** Nothing else — no auto-switch, no auto-create, no demotion, no button, no route.

Version **6.41.1** (PATCH). Removing the dead migrate route and button is a fix — the button could not render and the route could not succeed on Windows — so no observable behaviour a user could have relied on changes. The one deliberate behaviour change beyond a fix is `DELETE /admin/api/requests` now requiring a confirmation parameter and a local `Origin` (item 14); that is a hardening of a route whose only guard was a dismissable browser dialog, and the dashboard's Clear log button sends both.

## Every item in the brief

| # | Audit | What changed | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | F1 | Status route rewritten: `newDir` (where a migration would land) is now distinct from `currentDir` (the directory in use). The old `canMigrate` compared against `config_dir_path()`, which **is** `~/.fcc` for a legacy user, so it was always false. Nine route tests added: legacy-only, unhealthy legacy, dual-dir, `MCC_CONFIG_DIR`, fresh `~/.mcc`, loopback guard, and the migrate route's absence. | `api/admin_routes.py:960-1033`; `tests/api/test_admin_config_dir.py` (new, 8 tests) |
| 2 | F2 | A legacy home that fails the health probe is **still the config directory**. The `created`-after-failed-check branch is gone; the failure becomes a warning. `MCC_CONFIG_DIR` and the dual-dir warning are unchanged. | `config/paths.py:341-372`; `cli/commands.py:250-271`; tests: locked DB, truncated DB, `Settings()` raising, unreadable dir — `tests/config/test_paths.py:189-268` |
| 3 | F3 | `test_holder_detection_names_processes_on_windows` now patches `Path.home` like its siblings (and waits for the holding subprocess instead of racing it). A session-wide autouse guard fails any test that renames, creates or even *resolves* a config directory in the real home. The choke-point contract no longer does real-home I/O. | `tests/cli/test_migrate_config_dir.py:106-146`; `tests/conftest.py:113-235`; `tests/contracts/test_config_dir_is_single_sourced.py:66-84` |
| 4 | F4 | All 19 corrupted code spans repaired (README 10, USAGE 9 — `` `~/`.mcc` `` → `` `~/.mcc` ``, verified against `v6.39.2`). New content written: "Where your configuration lives", the legacy `~/.fcc` section, the `mcc-migrate` walkthrough (stop server + tray → run → start again), every refusal message and its remedy, `MCC_CONFIG_DIR`, `SERVER_LOG_RETAIN_FILES`. Drift contract extended with the two failure modes it could not see. | `docs/USAGE.md:153-266`; `README.md:530-588`; `.env.example:1-19,1296-1311`; `admin_static/index.html:1605-1628`; `tests/contracts/test_docs_reference_drift.py:479-573` (8 new checks, all 16 existing ones still pass) |
| 5 | F5 | `--force` **removed** — parser, signature, admin payload, docs. A refusal that advertises an escape hatch doing nothing is worse than a plain refusal, and there is no safe automatic behaviour to hang on it: when both directories exist only the user knows which holds the data. | `cli/migrate_config_dir.py:311-330,404` (removed); `api/admin_routes.py` (`MigrateConfigDirPayload` removed); `tests/cli/test_migrate_config_dir.py:304-320` |
| 6 | F6 | Dashboard migrate button and `POST /admin/api/migrate-config-dir` **removed**, with their CSS. The banner is one informational sentence naming the directory and the command. | `admin_static/admin.js:688-724`; `admin_static/admin.css` (removed); `api/admin_routes.py` (route removed); `tests/api/test_admin_config_dir.py:137-171` |
| 7 | F7 | `RESTORE.txt` now fails loudly instead of nesting: PowerShell tests for the target and `throw`s; POSIX uses `[ ! -e ]` plus `mv -T`. Both `Move-Item -Force` and a bare `mv` move the source *inside* an existing target — and a server left running across the migration recreates `~/.fcc` from its cached log path, so "the target exists" is the likely case. | `cli/migrate_config_dir.py:95-152`; `tests/cli/test_migrate_config_dir.py:355-376` |
| 8 | F8 | The sweep guard tests `len(rotated)`, not `retain_files` — it compared a small user setting against 100,000, so the documented "refuse to bulk-delete on a guess" protection never existed. `server_log_retain_files` gains `ge=0, le=100_000`. | `config/logging_config.py:180-190`; `config/settings.py:1093-1099`; `tests/config/test_logging_config.py:222-336` (5 new) |
| 9 | F9 | Per-entrypoint smoke tests: every `[project.scripts]`/`[project.gui-scripts]` target resolves; `serve`/`init`/`compact_log` register the request-log path *before* the command body runs; `mcc-migrate` needs none; the tray provably never builds the app in-process; no launcher or catalogue module touches the store. | `tests/cli/test_entrypoint_request_log_bootstrap.py` (new, 47 tests) |
| 10 | F10 | The `new_home.exists()` check is re-read in the same step as `os.replace`. Reserving the name with `mkdir(exist_ok=False)` would be worse — a crash between reservation and rename leaves an empty `~/.mcc` that then wins resolution forever. The residual window can only swallow an *empty* directory; a non-empty one is refused by the rename on every platform. Reasoning is written down at the call site. | `cli/migrate_config_dir.py:359-379`; `tests/cli/test_migrate_config_dir.py:271-301` |
| 11 | F11 | Holder detection matches `mcc-`/`fcc-`/the package name instead of `python`, `pythonw` and `uv`. A list a user is told to "close and re-run" is a list they may act on. | `cli/migrate_config_dir.py:56-84,175-182,196-198`; `tests/cli/test_migrate_config_dir.py:325-352` |
| 12 | F12 | The refusal is now true on every OS: `mcc-migrate` probes the tray's `desktop.lock` (never creating it) and `GET /health` on the port the legacy `.env` configures, and refuses while either answers. On POSIX `os.rename` succeeds with open handles, so this is what makes the documented promise real. | `cli/migrate_config_dir.py:205-283,351-357`; `config/paths.py:52-57` (`DESKTOP_LOCK_FILENAME`, now single-sourced); `tests/cli/test_migrate_config_dir.py:186-268` |
| 13 | F13 | `.env.example` says `~/.mcc` (5 mentions) and gains a header explaining the legacy directory and `MCC_CONFIG_DIR`; `index.html:1462`/`:3377` WSL text fixed; 46 `~/.fcc` mentions in module docstrings updated. `.fcc-tmp`/`.fcc-backup`/`model_providers.fcc` kept and each documented at its definition — renaming them would orphan real files on users' disks. New contract scans `.env.example` and the dashboard assets for bare `.fcc`. | `config/atomic_json.py:19-25`, `config/claude_settings.py:15-20`, `cli/launchers/codex.py:178-186`; `tests/contracts/test_config_dir_is_single_sourced.py:87-149` |
| 14 | F14 | Migrate route removed (item 6). `DELETE /admin/api/requests` now requires `?confirm=delete-all-request-log-rows` **and** a local `Origin` header — browsers attach one to every non-GET, `curl -X DELETE` does not. Read routes still accept a missing `Origin`. A `window.confirm()` in a page the caller need never load was not a guard. | `api/admin_routes.py:368-403,2575-2590`; `admin_static/admin.js:12238,12250-12253`; `tests/api/test_admin_requests.py:260-338` (5 new) |
| 15 | F15 | `CHECKPOINT.md` deleted. | removed |
| 16 | F16 | A legacy alias whose canonical name the Save writes is retired instead of preserved, so the `.env` cannot end up holding both `FCC_OPEN_BROWSER` and `MCC_OPEN_BROWSER`. Derived from `AliasChoices`, so it cannot go stale. | `config/admin/persistence.py:311-368`; `tests/config/test_env_aliases.py:60-95` |
| 17 | F17 | The provisional resolution published before the health probe is now the correctly resolved directory (`MCC_CONFIG_DIR` → `~/.mcc` → `~/.fcc` → `~/.mcc`) rather than `~/.fcc` unconditionally. | `config/paths.py:381-410`; `tests/config/test_paths.py:270-330` |
| 18 | audit (d) | The 6 PowerShell installer cases **now pass** rather than skip. Three real fixture bugs: the fake `uv` never answered `uv tool dir` (exit 59), its shim list was missing 6 commands the release publishes, and the `Get-FileHash` double returned a hash matching neither the feed nor the file. Three cases skip under Windows PowerShell 5.1 with a stated reason — verified by making the double `throw`: PS7 raises from it, 5.1 never enters it, so a successful checksum cannot be simulated there. | `tests/scripts/test_installers.py:610-626,670-694,860-870,879,909,995` |

## Tests

`uv run --offline pytest -q`: **9,362 passed, 43 skipped** (9,426 collected, +150 on `fork/main`).

The only failures on this machine are the 9 pre-existing local ones the brief lists (8 websearch/provider tests that read the developer's real `~/.fcc/.env`, plus `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`); they fail identically before this branch and Linux CI is green on them. `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` and one `test_desktop_rtk` case time out under xdist load and pass in isolation (226 passed).

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty check` (with `python-platform = "all"`): clean. No `# type: ignore` added.

commit.message:
fix(config-dir): only mcc-migrate ever moves ~/.fcc, and repair what 6.40.0 left behind

6.40.0 renamed the config directory to ~/.mcc and shipped the migration around
it half-finished. This finishes it, under one rule the user set: the ONLY way
~/.fcc becomes ~/.mcc is running mcc-migrate. Nothing else -- no auto-switch,
no auto-create, no demotion, no button.

Never demote a legacy home (F2). resolve_config_dir used to return a fresh,
empty ~/.mcc whenever the legacy health probe failed -- and any sqlite3 error
from a five-second read-only open counted, as did a Settings that would not
build for any reason at all. Rule 2 (~/.mcc wins whenever it exists) then made
that permanent: apparent total loss of keys and history from one locked
database. A failed check is now a warning about a directory that stays in use.

Remove the migrate button and route (F1, F5, F6, F14). The Get Started button
could never render -- canMigrate tested config_dir_path(), which IS ~/.fcc for
the user it existed for -- and on Windows it could not have succeeded anyway,
because the server serving the page holds the request log open inside the
directory being renamed. POST /admin/api/migrate-config-dir is gone with it: it
needed only loopback, and a missing Origin passed. The status route stays and
drives an informational banner. --force, parsed everywhere and read nowhere, is
gone too. There was no test for either route; there are nine now.

Make the refusal true on every OS (F12). "It refuses if a file is open" was a
Windows-only guarantee stated unconditionally; on POSIX the rename succeeds with
every handle open and the running server then recreates ~/.fcc from its cached
log path. mcc-migrate now probes the tray's desktop.lock and the configured
/health port first, on all platforms.

Also: RESTORE.txt commands fail loudly instead of nesting ~/.mcc inside a
recreated ~/.fcc (F7); the new-home check is re-read in the same step as the
rename (F10); holder detection names mcc-*/fcc-* processes instead of every
python.exe on the machine (F11); the rotated-log sweep guard tests what it
found rather than the cap, so the "refuse to bulk-delete on a guess" protection
now exists, and server_log_retain_files carries a 0..100000 range (F8); the
provisional resolution published before the health probe is the correct
directory rather than ~/.fcc unconditionally (F17); saving retires a legacy
FCC_* alias instead of leaving the .env holding both spellings (F16);
DELETE /admin/api/requests requires an explicit confirmation and a local Origin
(F14); CHECKPOINT.md is deleted (F15).

Tests: a session-wide guard fails any test that resolves, renames or creates a
config directory in the real home -- tests/cli/test_migrate_config_dir.py had a
case that ran mcc-migrate against the developer's own machine (F3). Per-entrypoint
smoke tests pin that every console script either registers the request-log path
or provably never opens a store (F9). The six PowerShell installer cases that
failed locally now pass: the fake uv did not answer `uv tool dir`, its shim list
was stale, and the Get-FileHash double returned a hash matching nothing. Three
of them skip under Windows PowerShell 5.1 with a reason (F18).

Docs: repair all 19 code spans a mechanical .fcc->.mcc rename corrupted, and
write the content the rename removed -- a legacy ~/.fcc section, the mcc-migrate
walkthrough, MCC_CONFIG_DIR and SERVER_LOG_RETAIN_FILES -- in README, USAGE, the
in-dashboard Guide and .env.example (F4, F13). The docs-drift contract gains
checks for both failure modes it could not see: a code span broken by a rename,
and a user-facing name that is documented nowhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsSZ8AQXV1XKgKkgYBU5UT

test(isolation): isolate the web-search analytics store, and blame the right test

The real-home guard fired on CI, where no config directory exists at all: the
suite created a real ``~/.mcc``. ``WebSearchAnalytics`` defaults to
``<config dir>/logs/websearch.db`` and builds that directory on construction,
and unlike the request log it was never isolated -- so on a developer machine it
wrote a real ``websearch.db`` into their config directory, and on a machine with
neither directory it created the one that then outranks a legacy ``~/.fcc``
for good. It now points at ``tmp_path`` like every other store.

The guard itself compared a directory listing before and after each test, which
under xdist blames whichever three workers happened to be mid-test rather than
the one that did it. It now intercepts the operations instead --
``Path.mkdir``/``os.mkdir``/``os.makedirs`` alongside ``os.replace``/``os.rename``
-- so the failure lands on the call that would have done the damage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsSZ8AQXV1XKgKkgYBU5UT

fix(tests): the real-home guard must know which directories it is guarding

Three corrections after CI ran the guard on a machine with no config directory
at all:

* ``_under_real_home`` meant "anywhere under the user profile", and on Windows
  pytest's own ``tmp_path`` lives under ``AppData/Local/Temp`` -- so every
  correctly isolated directory looked like a violation. It now means the three
  config directories themselves and anything inside them.
* ``ApplicationRuntime._start_messaging_workflow`` calls ``os.makedirs`` on
  ``<config dir>/agent_workspace``; isolated like the analytics store, lazily,
  so a test that redirects the config dir itself still gets its own answer.
* ``DesktopController.show_window`` persists ``desktop.json`` into the config
  directory, so that test was writing into the developer's real one. It
  redirects HOME like its siblings now.
